prov_binh_thuy.name: Bình Thủy
prov_binh_thuy.lore: A low green headland of grass and bamboo over the strait, the island's door to the mainland. Its people are ferry hands, rope-makers and innkeepers, many of them born somewhere else, and they live by Bình Thủy Môn's crossing. Every dusk the green lanterns on the sect's mast are lit, and a homesick traveller can read the name of his own village among them.

prov_p122.name: Bối Sa
prov_p122.lore: Flat grass and dry steppe running down to a white shell beach. Its fishers and shell-gatherers trade old shell money for small things and new shells to the mainland. A warm pool behind the dunes is where the shell-sorters soak their hands after the cold season's work.

prov_p123.name: Lãng Thạch
prov_p123.lore: Grassy shore and bamboo thickets around the split sea stack of Wave Rock. The village answers to Bình Thủy Môn and lives by fishing and by rowing visitors into the sea cave of old Cô Phàm charts. Great claw crabs come up out of the surf onto the grass, and the fishers count them a worse nuisance than storms.

prov_p124.name: Dương Liễu
prov_p124.lore: Dunes and coastal grass held in place by long rows of willows, with forest on the higher ground behind. The villagers fish and tend their willow rows, which they began planting after the sands buried Hải Khúc Trấn. Sand pythons lie up in the warm dunes, and children are taught to walk only on the willow paths.

prov_p125.name: Tình Sa
prov_p125.lore: A sunny river mouth of grass and bamboo, with the empty quays of Bích Không Cảng on its shore. Its fishers dry their catch on the sandbar beside the driftwood whale. A hot spring inland is where the islanders go to wash after a storm has passed, and they say it always rises clearer when the rain stops.

prov_p126.name: Nguyệt Loan
prov_p126.lore: Grass, bamboo and broad-leaf forest round the crescent cove where the island's fleets run from storms. Its people fish, mend boats and keep the storm shed hung with carved moons. Inland under the cassia trees runs a quiet spirit vein that Lạc Hà's disciples visit when they come over to the island.

prov_p37.name: Đàm Ảnh
prov_p37.lore: The broad grass and bamboo country around Đàm Ảnh Thành, the island's old Cô Phàm city on its river mouth. It lives by fish, trade and the painters who come to paint the sky upside down in the pool. A Water vein lies under the land nearby, and some say it is why the pool never ripples.

prov_p49.name: Tương Phùng
prov_p49.lore: Grass and dry steppe along the quay where the floating market of Tương Phùng Thị rides the tide. Its people are boatmen, stall-keepers and brokers who never know who the next ferry will bring. On the point beyond the market stands the empty hall of a school of wanderers that ended without an heir.

prov_p70.name: Xích Ngạn
prov_p70.lore: Red cliffs and rolling grass on the island's high coast, the land of the rust-red sails. Its people quarry and grind the red rock for pigment and fish from the cove below the cliff stair. On the headland stands the ruin of the hall where Cô Phàm's watchers once waited for the fleet.

prov_p71.name: Hải Yến
prov_p71.lore: Flat grass coast with patches of jungle, where the sea swallows nest under the town's double eaves. Families here own eaves the way others own fields and sell the nests to alchemists. In the jungle behind the town a Wood vein runs under the shade where the swallows hunt insects at dusk.

prov_p72.name: Triều Âm
prov_p72.lore: Jungle and grass around Lạc Hà Tông's own walled harbour at the river mouth, where the bored breakwater sings with the tide. Its people are sailors, customs men and fishers, and Lạc Hà's ships call here first. Crocodiles bask on the shoals upriver, and the city's boatmen keep to the far bank.

prov_r10_1.name: Tang Du
prov_r10_1.lore: High grass, forest and a strip of steppe on the island's sunset coast, where the last light lies longest. Its few villagers keep goats on the slopes and fish below the cliffs. Above the village lie the sand-choked lanes of Hải Khúc Trấn, a town the dunes walked over.

prov_r10_10.name: Thanh Đằng
prov_r10_10.lore: Deep inland jungle with no river and no coast, hung everywhere with rattan. Its villagers cut and split the canes and weave the baskets and ropes that the coast towns buy. Banyans stand so thick on the high ground that their roots make the paths.

prov_r10_11.name: Trầm Hương
prov_r10_11.lore: Jungle coast where old agarwood trees grow, the island's richest wood. Its town lives by the resin trade, and its finest kỳ nam wood goes to Lạc Hà's meditation halls as incense. Gatherers who go into the old groves mark their trees with knots of red cord, and stealing a marked tree is the worst crime the town knows.

prov_r10_12.name: Xướng Vãn
prov_r10_12.lore: Jungle and coastal grass on a low shore of the island's far end. Its fishing boats come in singing at dusk, as boats do all over Lạc Hà's lands, and the village keeps the song even in bad years. Wild plantain groves on the grass behind the beach feed the village through the lean season.

prov_r10_13.name: Hồng Thụ
prov_r10_13.lore: Jungle running down into a mangrove shore. Its villagers catch crabs, burn mangrove charcoal and gather the island's shellfish. Flying foxes the size of eagles roost in the jungle behind the village and strip its fruit trees at night.

prov_r10_14.name: Phương Lân
prov_r10_14.lore: Jungle and mangrove on a low shore that dips below the sea. Two fishing clans share the village and have never quarrelled, which the island thinks a wonder. Behind them lies a drowned forest of water pines, cut for boat timber that does not rot.

prov_r10_15.name: Nam Minh
prov_r10_15.lore: The island's jungle tip, where the mist rises off the deep sea and the mist leopards of Vụ Báo Lâm hunt inland. Its one village fishes the deep water off the point. No one goes inland by the leopards' paths, and Bình Thủy's ferrymen warn travellers away from them.

prov_r10_2.name: Ngưu Đẩu
prov_r10_2.lore: Rolling inland grass rising to forested heights, the highest farmland on the island. Its villagers raise water buffalo and say their herds were named after the stars over the hills. Spirit porcupines den in the forest above, and their quills are sold to the talisman makers of the mainland.

prov_r10_3.name: Mộ Sơn
prov_r10_3.lore: Inland hills of grass, bamboo and forest that turn purple at dusk. Its villagers grow tea on the slopes and graze cattle on the tops. A hot spring in the hills is said to make the greedy greedier and the honest clearer, and the villagers drink from it only at weddings.

prov_r10_4.name: Vọng Hương
prov_r10_4.lore: Grass and bamboo along the strait coast beside Bình Thủy's headland. Its fishers dry cuttlefish and sell it to the ferry passengers. Travellers fresh off the crossing wash the road off in its hot spring before they go on.

prov_r10_5.name: Lục Trúc
prov_r10_5.lore: Inland bamboo forest, with a little grass where the groves thin. Its people cut bamboo for houses, rafts and paper and dig the shoots in spring. Jade-scaled bamboo vipers live in the deepest groves, and cutters wear thick leggings of buffalo hide.

prov_r10_6.name: Trúc Phiệt
prov_r10_6.lore: Bamboo forest coming down to a sheltered coast. Its villagers build bamboo rafts and fish traps and float cut cane along the shore to the towns. The great grove inland is so old that no one has ever found its far edge on foot.

prov_r10_7.name: Lan Chu
prov_r10_7.lore: Bamboo and grass on a calm stretch of coast, the island's boatbuilding shore. Its town builds the light fishing boats of Cô Vụ Đảo and is famous for carving an orchid on each prow. Wild buffalo with iron-hard horns graze the grass behind the yards and must be driven off before the timber carts can pass.

prov_r10_8.name: Đê Hạ
prov_r10_8.lore: Low grass and bamboo on a shore that lies below the sea at high tide, kept dry by an earth dyke. Its people grow rice and raise fish in the ditches behind the dyke. Every year spirit sea turtles come ashore to lay their eggs on the beach outside it, and the villagers keep well clear.

prov_r10_9.name: Phong Sào
prov_r10_9.lore: Inland jungle with no river and no coast, the island's dark heart. Its villagers climb the tallest trees to take wild honey and wax. A Wood vein runs under the high canopy nearby, and the bees there are said to be larger and calmer than anywhere else.

prov_binh_thuy_hot_spring_1.name: Tha Hương Tuyền
prov_binh_thuy_hot_spring_1.look: A round warm pool in the grass behind the headland, rimmed with flat stones worn smooth by bathers and ringed by small wooden name boards.
prov_binh_thuy_hot_spring_1.lore: New disciples of Bình Thủy Môn bathe here on their first night and nail the name of their home village to a board beside the pool. It is said the water tastes faintly of whatever home the bather left.

prov_p122_hot_spring_1.name: Ôn Bối Trì
prov_p122_hot_spring_1.look: A shallow warm pool in the grass behind the dunes, its bottom white with old shells.
prov_p122_hot_spring_1.lore: The shell-gatherers of Bối Sa soak their cracked hands here after the cold season. They throw in one shell from every catch, so the floor rises a little every year.

prov_p123_beast_lair_1.name: Cự Ngao Chử
prov_p123_beast_lair_1.look: A flat of rough grass and tide pools behind the shore, pocked with burrows wide enough to swallow a goat.
prov_p123_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit crabs with claws as long as an arm come up out of the surf to burrow here. Their shells are hard enough to turn a blade, and the fishers of Lãng Thạch sell them to armourers on the mainland.

prov_p124_beast_lair_1.name: Sa Mãng Cương
prov_p124_beast_lair_1.look: A warm bare dune ridge beyond the willow rows, its sand marked with long curving trails.
prov_p124_beast_lair_1.lore: Sand pythons as thick as a man lie buried in the warm sand and take what walks over them. The villagers of Dương Liễu say the willows are the only thing the snakes will not cross.

prov_p125_hot_spring_1.name: Vũ Tễ Tuyền
prov_p125_hot_spring_1.look: A steaming pool in open grass that clouds over in wet weather and runs clear as glass when the rain stops.
prov_p125_hot_spring_1.lore: The islanders read the weather by it: when the pool clears, the storm is over. Fishers of Tình Sa will not put out until they have seen it clear.

prov_p126_spirit_vein_1.name: Quế Ảnh Mạch
prov_p126_spirit_vein_1.look: A grove of old cassia trees in the forest above the cove, where the moonlight falls through the leaves in sharp silver patches.
prov_p126_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the cassias, strongest on moonlit nights. Lạc Hà's disciples who come over to the island sit here when the moon is full and say the sea is quieter in their meridians.

prov_p37_spirit_vein_1.name: Tinh Di Mạch
prov_p37_spirit_vein_1.look: A hollow in the grass with a ring of still, dark pools, in which the stars can be seen to move across the night.
prov_p37_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Water vein runs under the land here, and the painters of Đàm Ảnh say it feeds the stillness of the city's pool. Its name comes from the old line about things changing and stars moving through the autumns.

prov_p37_minor_seat_p.name: Nhàn Vân Quán
prov_p37_minor_seat_p.look: A low abbey of grey roofs on the steppe shore, its long open galleries hung with silk scrolls of clouds that seem to drift when the sea wind moves them.
prov_p37_minor_seat_p.lore: Painters who came to Đàm Ảnh Thành for its pool founded the abbey in 905, under Lạc Hà Tông, and learned to paint with qi in the ink. Their scrolls can hold a reflection, hide a doorway or show a cloud that is not there. Every disciple must first paint the pool of Đàm Ảnh well enough that a heron tries to land on it.

sect.name: Nhàn Vân Quán
sect.craft: painting cultivation: living scrolls and mirror images

prov_p49_spirit_vein_1.name: Bình Tung Mạch
prov_p49_spirit_vein_1.look: A shallow green pond in the grass behind the market, its surface thick with duckweed that drifts in rings with no wind to move it.
prov_p49_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Water vein lies under the pond, and its qi wanders like the duckweed, never strongest in the same place two days running. Bình Thủy's disciples say it suits their sect better than any steady vein would.

prov_p49_ruin_2.name: Phiêu Bồng Quán
prov_p49_ruin_2.look: A small roofless abbey on the steppe point, its walls whole but its doors gone and its courtyard full of wind-blown grass.
prov_p49_ruin_2.lore: Wanderers who would not settle founded a small school here in 860 and taught that a cultivator should belong to no place. In 1102 its last master died with no disciple willing to stay, and he left its books to Bình Thủy Môn. The abbey has stood empty since, and travellers waiting for the ferry still sleep in it.

prov_p70_beast_lair_1.name: Sài Quần Nguyên
prov_p70_beast_lair_1.look: Open red-earthed grass above the cliffs, crossed by worn trails and littered with old bones.
prov_p70_beast_lair_1.lore: Packs of rust-red spirit dholes hunt the grass inland of Xích Ngạn, the colour of the rock they run over. The townsfolk drive their goats in at dusk and keep fires on the cliff stair.

prov_p70_ruin_2.name: Vọng Phàm Quán
prov_p70_ruin_2.gloss: Abbey of the Watch for Sails
prov_p70_ruin_2.look: A broken hall of red stone on the steppe headland, its roof fallen in and a stone platform facing the open sea.
prov_p70_ruin_2.lore: Cô Phàm Các built this watch hall in 430 for its watchers to call the fleet home. After the fleet was lost in 705 the last watchers kept the vigil for three more years, then went down to Xích Ngạn and did not come back. The townsfolk say a lamp is sometimes seen on the platform on stormy nights.

prov_p71_spirit_vein_1.name: Lục Âm Mạch
prov_p71_spirit_vein_1.look: A dim stand of jungle behind the town where the canopy closes overhead and the air is cool and green even at noon.
prov_p71_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Wood vein runs under the shade, and the sea swallows of Hải Yến hunt the insects that swarm over it at dusk. The town's nest harvesters rest here at midday and say they never grow sick.

prov_p72_beast_lair_1.name: Ngạc Ngư Chử
prov_p72_beast_lair_1.look: Muddy jungle shoals on the river upstream of the city, where long grey backs lie motionless in the shallows.
prov_p72_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit crocodiles bask here, some longer than a river boat. Triều Âm's boatmen keep to the far bank and throw them the fish offal from the market, which keeps them fat and lazy.

prov_r10_1_village_1.name: Tang Du Thôn
prov_r10_1_village_1.look: A few stone houses on the steppe shore, their doors all turned to the sunset and goat pens on the slope behind.
prov_r10_1_village_1.lore: The village is named for the old saying that the setting sun among the mulberries and elms is late, but not too late. Its people keep goats and fish, and old islanders come here to live out their last years facing the evening.

prov_r10_1_spirit_vein_2.name: Tà Dương Mạch
prov_r10_1_spirit_vein_2.look: A low grassy rise where the evening light falls level across a field of warm, ochre stones.
prov_r10_1_spirit_vein_2.lore: An Earth vein runs under the rise, strongest in the hour of the evening glow, which suits Lạc Hà's arts. The sect's disciples on the island come here at dusk to cultivate.

prov_r10_1_ruin_3.name: Hải Khúc Trấn
prov_r10_1_ruin_3.look: The tops of walls and a gate arch sticking out of drifted sand on a grassy coastal hill, the lanes between them filled to the windowsills.
prov_r10_1_ruin_3.lore: Fishers built the town on a bend of the coast in 430. Storm after storm blew the beach sand up the hill into its wells and lanes, and in 748 the last families left it. Two years later the people of Dương Liễu began planting willows on their own dunes, so that the same would not happen to them.

prov_r10_10_village_1.name: Thanh Đằng Thôn
prov_r10_10_village_1.look: Stilted houses in a jungle clearing, their walls woven of split rattan and bundles of green cane stacked under every floor.
prov_r10_10_village_1.lore: The villagers cut the rattan of the inland jungle and weave the baskets, ropes and fish traps the coast towns buy. A child here learns to split cane before it learns to count.

prov_r10_10_forest_2.name: Bàn Căn Lâm
prov_r10_10_forest_2.look: A high jungle of giant banyans whose hanging roots have grown into trunks, so that one tree stands like a grove.
prov_r10_10_forest_2.lore: The paths through it run along the roots, never on the ground. Rattan cutters say one banyan here has swallowed a whole hut, and that its roof can still be seen inside the trunk.

prov_r10_11_town_1.name: Trầm Hương Trấn
prov_r10_11_town_1.look: A small walled town on the jungle shore whose air is heavy with incense smoke from the resin sheds along its quay.
prov_r10_11_town_1.lore: The town lives by the agarwood of the jungle behind it, graded and sold by weight in its sheds. Its best kỳ nam goes to Lạc Hà Tông's meditation halls, and a merchant who sells false agarwood here is banished from the island.

prov_r10_11_forest_2.name: Kỳ Nam Lâm
prov_r10_11_forest_2.gloss: Forest of the Kỳ Nam Agarwood
prov_r10_11_forest_2.look: An old jungle of tall pale-barked trees, many tied with knots of red cord and scarred where resin has been cut.
prov_r10_11_forest_2.lore: The finest agarwood, kỳ nam, forms only in old wounded trees here, and a single piece can buy a house. Each gatherer marks his trees with red cord, and the cords are older than most of the gatherers.

prov_r10_12_village_1.name: Xướng Vãn Thôn
prov_r10_12_village_1.look: A fishing village of thatched houses on a grassy shore, its boats drawn up in a long row with their bows toward the sunset.
prov_r10_12_village_1.lore: Its boats come in singing at dusk, as fishing boats do all over Lạc Hà's lands. In 803, when the boats fell silent after Chiết Kích Nguyên, the village kept silent for a year, and it still sings one verse fewer than its neighbours.

prov_r10_12_forest_2.name: Ba Tiêu Lâm
prov_r10_12_forest_2.look: A thicket of wild plantains on the coastal grass, their broad torn leaves rattling in the sea wind.
prov_r10_12_forest_2.lore: The wild plantains feed the village in lean years, and rain on the leaves can be heard from the beach. Children are sent to gather the fruit and told never to go past the last tree.

prov_r10_13_village_1.name: Hồng Thụ Thôn
prov_r10_13_village_1.look: Houses on stilts among the mangrove roots, joined by plank walks, with charcoal kilns smoking on the firmer ground behind.
prov_r10_13_village_1.lore: Its people catch mud crabs, gather shellfish and burn mangrove charcoal for the island's smiths. They cut only every third tree, so the mangrove will keep the sea out.

prov_r10_13_beast_lair_2.name: Phi Hồ Lâm
prov_r10_13_beast_lair_2.look: A patch of jungle whose trees hang thick with dark folded shapes by day, and roar with wings at dusk.
prov_r10_13_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit fruit bats as broad as eagles roost here in thousands and strip the island's orchards at night. A bitten hunter runs a fever for a month, and the villagers leave the roost alone.

prov_r10_14_village_1.name: Phương Lân Thôn
prov_r10_14_village_1.look: A fishing village on a low shore with a single long boat shed shared down the middle by two clans.
prov_r10_14_village_1.lore: Two fishing clans have shared the village since it was founded and have never once gone to the elders with a quarrel. The island says it is the only village where a borrowed net always comes back mended.

prov_r10_14_forest_2.name: Thủy Tùng Lâm
prov_r10_14_forest_2.look: A drowned forest below the level of the sea, where straight water pines stand knee-deep in black water beside the mangrove.
prov_r10_14_forest_2.lore: The wood of the water pine does not rot, and the boatwrights of Lan Chu pay well for it. Cutters go in only at low tide, by boat, and leave before the water rises.

prov_r10_15_village_1.name: Nam Minh Thôn
prov_r10_15_village_1.look: A small fishing village on the jungle point, facing a sea so deep it shows dark blue right up to the rocks.
prov_r10_15_village_1.lore: Its fishers take the deep-water fish no one else on the island can reach. They never go inland, since the mist leopards of Vụ Báo Lâm hunt the paths behind the village.

prov_r10_2_village_1.name: Ngưu Đẩu Thôn
prov_r10_2_village_1.look: A hill village of grey roofs on open grass, its buffalo pens ringed with stone walls.
prov_r10_2_village_1.lore: The villagers raise water buffalo and name their herds after the stars of the Ox and the Dipper, which stand over the hills in autumn. The old line says a dragon light once shot up toward those stars, and the village children still watch for it.

prov_r10_2_beast_lair_2.name: Hào Trư Lĩnh
prov_r10_2_beast_lair_2.look: A forested ridge whose paths are littered with black and white quills as long as a forearm.
prov_r10_2_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit porcupines den here and can shoot their quills across a clearing. The talisman makers of the mainland buy the quills as pens, and the hunters who gather them wear buffalo-hide coats.

prov_r10_3_village_1.name: Mộ Sơn Thôn
prov_r10_3_village_1.look: A village of tea terraces on a grassy hillside that turns purple at dusk.
prov_r10_3_village_1.lore: Its villagers grow tea and graze cattle on the hilltops. They pick the tea only in the hour before sunset, and Lạc Hà's disciples say it is the only tea that tastes of the evening glow.

prov_r10_3_hot_spring_2.name: Tham Tuyền
prov_r10_3_hot_spring_2.look: A small hot spring in a cleft of the grassy hills, its water bright and sweet-smelling.
prov_r10_3_hot_spring_2.lore: The old saying holds that whoever drinks from the spring of greed turns greedy, and that a clean heart only finds it refreshing. The villagers drink from it only at weddings, to show the families have nothing to hide.

prov_r10_4_village_1.name: Vọng Hương Thôn
prov_r10_4_village_1.look: A fishing village on the strait coast, its racks of drying cuttlefish lined up facing the mainland across the water.
prov_r10_4_village_1.lore: The villagers dry cuttlefish and sell it to ferry passengers, many of them homesick. On clear days the mainland can be seen from the beach, and the old men sit and look at it.

prov_r10_4_hot_spring_2.name: Tẩy Trần Tuyền
prov_r10_4_hot_spring_2.gloss: Spring that Washes off the Dust
prov_r10_4_hot_spring_2.look: A warm spring in the grass a short walk from the ferry road, with a bathhouse of bamboo built over it.
prov_r10_4_hot_spring_2.lore: Travellers fresh off the strait crossing wash the road off here before going on. Bình Thủy Môn pays for the bathhouse, and a newcomer's first bath is free.

prov_r10_5_village_1.name: Lục Trúc Thôn
prov_r10_5_village_1.look: Bamboo houses deep in a bamboo forest, with paper pulp vats steaming in the clearings.
prov_r10_5_village_1.lore: Its people cut bamboo for houses and rafts, dig shoots in spring and make a coarse paper that Nam Phố Đường buys for practice talismans. The old line about green bamboo in a garden is painted over the village gate.

prov_r10_5_beast_lair_2.name: Bích Lân Lâm
prov_r10_5_beast_lair_2.look: The deepest groves of the bamboo forest, where green shapes lie along the canes and drop at a footstep.
prov_r10_5_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit bamboo vipers as green as the canes live here, and their bite stops a heart in minutes. Cutters wear buffalo-hide leggings and tap the canes ahead with a long pole.

prov_r10_6_village_1.name: Trúc Phiệt Thôn
prov_r10_6_village_1.look: A coastal village where bamboo rafts are lashed together on the beach and stacked cane floats moored in the shallows.
prov_r10_6_village_1.lore: Its villagers build rafts and fish traps and float cut bamboo along the shore to the towns. A raft here is lashed with rattan from Thanh Đằng and lasts three seasons.

prov_r10_6_forest_2.name: Vạn Can Lâm
prov_r10_6_forest_2.look: An endless bamboo forest whose canes stand so close that the light inside is green and the wind sounds like rain.
prov_r10_6_forest_2.lore: No one has walked to its far edge, and cutters work only its rim. Bình Thủy's disciples train their footwork on the canes, running along the tops without touching the ground.

prov_r10_7_town_1.name: Lan Chu Trấn
prov_r10_7_town_1.look: A small walled town on a calm shore whose slips are crowded with half-built fishing boats, each with an orchid carved on the prow.
prov_r10_7_town_1.lore: The town builds the light fishing boats of Cô Vụ Đảo from bamboo and water pine. The orchid on each prow is the builder's mark, and a boat without one will not be bought.

prov_r10_7_beast_lair_2.name: Thiết Giác Nguyên
prov_r10_7_beast_lair_2.look: Open grass behind the boatyards, churned into wallows and grazed short by heavy beasts.
prov_r10_7_beast_lair_2.lore: Wild spirit buffalo with horns hard as iron graze here and charge anything that comes near their calves. The town's carters drive them off with drums before the timber carts go through.

prov_r10_8_village_1.name: Đê Hạ Thôn
prov_r10_8_village_1.look: A village of rice fields and fish ditches below a long earth dyke, the sea higher than its roofs at high tide.
prov_r10_8_village_1.lore: Its people grow rice and raise fish behind the dyke and send every household to mend it after a storm. A crack in the dyke is called before a fire.

prov_r10_8_beast_lair_2.name: Hải Quy Chử
prov_r10_8_beast_lair_2.look: A stretch of grassy shore pitted with great sand nests, each as wide as a cart.
prov_r10_8_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit sea turtles come ashore each year to lay their eggs, and the mothers bite through a boat's side. The villagers of Đê Hạ keep away until the young have gone to sea.

prov_r10_9_village_1.name: Phong Sào Thôn
prov_r10_9_village_1.look: A village in a jungle clearing, its houses hung with wax combs and long bamboo ladders leaning on the tallest trees.
prov_r10_9_village_1.lore: Its villagers climb the jungle giants to take wild honey and wax, which they trade to the alchemists of Hải Yến. A honey hunter sings to the bees as he climbs, and no one else may use his song.

prov_r10_9_spirit_vein_2.name: Thúy Cái Mạch
prov_r10_9_spirit_vein_2.look: A high knoll in the jungle where the canopy closes into one green roof, humming with large slow bees.
prov_r10_9_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Wood vein runs under the knoll, and the bees over it are larger and calmer than anywhere else on the island. The honey hunters of Phong Sào leave its combs alone and say the vein belongs to the bees.
